children: UniCredit
has been weighing a possible increase of its 9% stake in Generali
, four people close to the matter said, as Italy's second-biggest bank and the country's largest insurer discuss new commercial accords.
The Generali investment has so far been the only move by UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel in Italy's fast-consolidating banking market.
The veteran dealmaker has just secured control of Germany's Commerzbank
, and says UniCredit will grow its domestic market share without any major acquisitions.
Meanwhile, the Generali stake has positioned UniCredit as a counterweight to its main rival Intesa Sanpaolo
- which looks set to become the biggest Generali shareholder through a takeover of Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS)
Two of the four people said UniCredit could raise its Generali holding towards the 13.4% stake which is expected to pass from MPS into Intesa's hands.
The outcome of UniCredit's deliberations remains uncertain.
UniCredit and Generali both declined to comment.
By exercising significant influence over Generali, without control, Intesa can book the insurer's profits in its earnings in proportion to the stake, under international accounting rules.
Independent of its Generali stake coming from the MPS deal, Intesa has also built a further 3% stake in the insurer, which it has said it will dispose of.
Intesa CEO Carlo Messina has said he would be happy for UniCredit and Generali to find ways to generate profits together.
UniCredit first unveiled a 4.1% Generali stake , before building it up to the current 9.05%. Crossing 10% requires supervisory approval.
UniCredit and Generali, which already partner in eastern Europe, have been discussing closer commercial ties.
On November 9, Orcel said it was up to Generali to decide whether to accept UniCredit's help, adding that he hoped an agreement could be reached in the coming months.
He has repeatedly said such partnerships do not require UniCredit to control Generali, or a formal combination.

Orcel last week put the value of closer cooperation between UniCredit and Generali at €1.5-€2.0 billion ($1.6-$2.2 billion), with Generali remaining independent and simply agreeing to "innovative" forms of  partnership.
A day later, Generali CEO Philippe Donnet said the insurer agrees with Orcel's view of the value the two companies can generate together.($1 = 0.9136 euros)
